title: Sándor Márai's birth chart
metaDescription: Sándor Márai's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 21.1° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 21.1° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 21.1° Aries, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Jupiter. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 27.1° Pisces, Venus at 5.7° Gemini, Mars at 2.6° Aries. Mercury in a water sign reads as thought steeped in tone and memory; Venus in an air sign reads as attraction that begins as conversation; Mars in a fire sign reads as effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Jupiter in the same degree of the zodiac from Uranus, 1.7° off exact. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct. Behind it, Mars square Saturn at 2.5°, and Mercury square Neptune at 2.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, five placements stand out. The Sun in Aries at 21.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Pisces at 27.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Aries at 2.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 10.5° is in domicile; Saturn in Capricorn at 5.0° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 fire, 3 air, 2 earth, 1 water by element and 7 mutable, 3 cardinal by modality. A fire-weighted chart runs hot at the start line — initiative is its native language. Jupiter and Uranus were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 11.7°.
